claims.claim: An alleged optimum has a linear-time verifiable certificate, even for arbitrary signed entries.
claims.evidence: Let q=min(m,n). A claimed L is optimal exactly when L is feasible and every length l>L is infeasible. Feasibility of L is checked by scanning its at most mn placements; one violating square certifies each larger length's infeasibility. A two-dimensional prefix table makes every square-sum query constant-time, so preprocessing plus all checks takes O(mn+q)=O(mn) arithmetic/word operations. Signs do not affect this equivalence. The L=0 convention correctly certifies that no positive length is feasible. This is a word-operation result, not a bit-complexity bound.
claims.search_method: Proved the certificate acceptance condition in both directions and exhaustively checked all alleged lengths on 7,845 small signed matrix/threshold instances using exact integers.

claims.claim: There is an exact output-sensitive search algorithm whose worst-case time is O(mn min(m,n)).
claims.evidence: Descending inspection is correct without any monotonicity assumption: all lengths larger than the first feasible length have already received explicit violations. For m>=n=q and d=q-L, testing length n-t has at most (m-n+t+1)(t+1) placements, giving the displayed sum through t=d. This is O(mn+(m-n+1)(d+1)^2+(d+1)^3), hence O(mnq) in the worst case and O(mn) for constant d. When L=0 the displayed sum merely includes one harmless extra t=q term.
claims.search_method: Derived the placement count directly and compared descending search with brute-force optimum on 7,845 exact signed instances; the observed inspection count was also checked against the stated output-sensitive sum.

claims.claim: Feasibility can alternate at every side length, and the natural no-revisit greedy extension is incorrect.
claims.evidence: In the alternating-row family, an even-length interval in the only nonzero row sums to zero. For odd length, such an interval sums to either 1 or -1, while squares below that row sum to zero; therefore F_l=0 for even l and F_l=1 for odd l. With k=0, feasibility alternates at every consecutive length. For the greedy example, F_2=4>1 and F_1=2>1, so the true answer under the draft's convention is 0. A left-to-right no-revisit scan nevertheless first sees the safe side-2 sum 1, decreases only upon the later sum 4, and can then miss the earlier side-1 violation 2.
claims.witness: For k=0, use the n by n matrix with first row (1,-1,1,-1,...) and all other entries zero. For the greedy failure use k=1 and [[2,1,1],[-3,1,1]]; its side-2 sums are [1,4], while the skipped earlier side-1 entry is 2.
claims.search_method: Proved the interval-sum cases by parity, evaluated the 2-by-3 witness exactly, and checked the alternating family for every n from 1 through 32.

claims.claim: The O(mn) endpoint is achievable for two nontrivial signed separable classes: multiplicative rank one and additive separability.
claims.evidence: For A_ij=u_i v_j, every l-square sum is the product of an l-window sum of u and an l-window sum of v. A bilinear function on the two resulting intervals attains its maximum at one of the four endpoint products. With a pivot p, the same argument evaluates all four corner products divided by p; dividing each corner before taking the maximum also handles p<0. The pivot identities recognize nonzero rank-one matrices, and the all-zero case is trivial. For A_ij=u_i+v_j, the sum is l(X+Y), so only the two maximum window sums are needed. Scanning all windows for every l costs q(m+n)<=2mn, and both recognition tests cost O(mn).
claims.witness: Representative signed rank-one factors u=(-2,1,2), v=(2,-1,0,2) give rows (-4,2,0,-4), (2,-1,0,2), and (4,-2,0,4). Representative additive factors u=(-1,0,1), v=(1,-1,0,1) also produce both signs.
claims.search_method: Proved both separation identities and recognition conditions. Exhaustively checked 78,125 signed 3-by-4 rank-one factorizations, including negative pivots, and 2,187 signed additive factorizations with exact integer arithmetic.

claims.claim: A thresholded max-plus-convolution scan embeds exactly into matrices supported on one row.
claims.evidence: For l=B-t and horizontal start s, the supported-row square sum telescopes to p_{s+B-t}-p_s. Setting i=s and j=t-s makes this C+x_i+y_j exactly when i,j are valid convolution indices. If i is invalid, the start prefix is H; if j is invalid, the endpoint prefix is -H. The stated bounds make every invalid window negative, whereas every valid value is at least 1. Zero squares below the first row therefore cannot change the maximum, yielding F_{B-t}=C+c_t. Feasibility at threshold C+K is consequently equivalent to c_t<=K throughout the encoded high-length range, and the largest feasible encoded length corresponds to the least passing t.
claims.witness: For x=(1,-2), y=(3,0), take B=8, C=7, middle prefix values zero, and first matrix row (3,9,-11,0,0,-11,18,3), with all other rows zero. Then c=(4,1,-2) and (F_8,F_7,F_6)=(11,8,5)=C+c. At K=1, threshold 8 gives answer 7.
claims.search_method: Checked the telescoping indices and all invalid-index cases symbolically. Exhaustively tested 22,836 vector pairs for N=1 through 4, thirteen thresholds per pair, and deliberately large unequal choices for the three arbitrary prefix values, all with exact integers.

claims.claim: If integer bit lengths are unbounded and bit operations are charged, an O(mn) bound independent of bit length is impossible.
claims.evidence: A 1-by-1 instance requires deciding whether its entry a is at most k. In an explicit-binary bit-cost model, choose a=k=2^(B-1). For every lower position r, replacing a by k+2^r changes the correct answer while changing only that bit. Correctness on the equality instance therefore requires ruling out all B-1 alternatives, giving Omega(B) worst-case bit cost. Thus a bound O(mn) independent of bit length is impossible, although this says nothing against O(mn) word operations.
claims.witness: For each B>=2, compare a=k=2^(B-1) with the alternatives a_r=2^(B-1)+2^r for 0<=r<B-1. Equality makes side length 1 feasible, while every alternative makes it infeasible.
claims.search_method: Applied a deterministic bit-probe adversary argument and exactly instantiated all 2,016 lower-bit alternatives for bit lengths 2 through 64.

target_evidence: The exact target requests a general O(mn) algorithm for arbitrary signed matrices or a meaningful impossibility result at the corresponding endpoint. The draft explicitly supplies neither for the usual bounded-word/unit-cost formulation. Its verifier, O(mn min(m,n)) search, nonmonotonicity examples, separable special cases, and convolution embedding are correct and material partial progress. Claim 5 is only the generic input-length obstruction for unbounded explicit integers; it is much coarser than, and mismatched to, the substantive word-RAM endpoint, so it does not fully resolve the target. The final writeup expressly says that endpoint remains unresolved and labels its resolution PARTIAL, making the claimed resolution accurate rather than overstated or understated.
